name: Docker Engine
description: Umbrella term for the daemon-plus-runtime stack that runs containers on a host: dockerd (HTTP/REST API + image/volume/network management) on top of containerd (lifecycle, snapshotters) on top of an OCI runtime (runc by default). The product surface a Linux user installs as the `docker` package or via Docker Desktop. The 'engine' leaf focuses on dockerd and its on-host responsibilities; runtime internals (runc/containerd) are catalogued in the docker/runtime leaf.

name: dockerd
description: The persistent Docker daemon process. Listens on a Unix socket (default `/var/run/docker.sock`) for the Docker Engine API; configurable to also listen on TCP for remote clients. Reads `/etc/docker/daemon.json` at startup; flag-form configuration overrides JSON. Reload-via-SIGHUP semantics for some keys; full restart required for others. The first thing to inspect when containers refuse to start, the API socket is denied, or images won't pull.

name: containerd
description: The container lifecycle daemon Docker delegates to for create/start/stop/exec. Below dockerd; above runc. Owns its own snapshotters, content store, and image store. Reachable on its own socket (`/run/containerd/containerd.sock`). When you see 'containerd image store', this is the storage backend; when you see 'containerd snapshotter', this is the per-driver layer manager (overlayfs, native, btrfs, zfs, devmapper). Detailed surface lives in docker/runtime.

name: containerd shim
description: A small per-container process that decouples a container's lifecycle from the containerd daemon. Lets containerd be restarted without killing every container. Standard shim is `containerd-shim-runc-v2`; alternative shims (kata, gVisor, Wasm runtimes) implement the v2 shim API and ship as `containerd-shim-<name>-v1` binaries placed on PATH. Picked via `--runtime <fully-qualified-name>` on `docker run` or via daemon.json `runtimes` map.

name: runc
description: The default OCI runtime — a lightweight CLI that spawns and runs containers from an OCI bundle (`config.json` + rootfs). Invoked by the containerd shim. Exit code 137 = OOM (128+9). Fully detailed in docker/runtime; here only the engine-perspective: it's the thing that actually applies namespaces/cgroups/capabilities/seccomp to a container's pid 1.

name: crun
description: runc-compatible alternative OCI runtime written in C. Faster startup, lower memory than runc. Drop-in via daemon.json `runtimes` entry pointing `path` to the `crun` binary, then `docker run --runtime crun`. Equivalent surface to runc (config.json, capabilities, etc.); choice is mostly performance/footprint.

name: docker-init (tini)
description: Minimal pid1-replacement injected via `--init` (or daemon-wide `init: true` in daemon.json). Reaps zombies and forwards signals so processes that don't expect to be pid1 don't leak children or ignore SIGTERM. Path configurable via `init-path`. Solves the 'docker stop hangs for 10s then SIGKILLs' symptom for naive entrypoints.

name: docker CLI
description: User-facing client (`docker`) that talks to dockerd over the API. Stateless beyond the per-user `~/.docker/config.json`. Honors `DOCKER_HOST`, `DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY`, `DOCKER_CERT_PATH`, `DOCKER_CONFIG`, `DOCKER_CONTEXT`, `DOCKER_API_VERSION`, `DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM`, `DOCKER_BUILDKIT`. When `docker ps` returns 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon', the CLI couldn't reach the socket — daemon-side, not client-side.

name: docker context
description: A named profile bundling endpoint URL + TLS materials, used to switch the CLI between local and remote daemons (or between rootful and rootless dockerds). `docker context ls` / `docker context use`. `DOCKER_CONTEXT` env var picks one for a single command. Avoids the foot-gun of forgetting `DOCKER_HOST` between shells.

name: dockerd plugin API
description: Pluggable extension surface for storage, volume, network, log, authorization. Plugins registered via `docker plugin install` or via daemon-side `authorization-plugins` config. Source of failures when a third-party volume/log driver is misconfigured (daemon won't start, or `docker volume create -d <plugin>` errors).

name: Container
description: A running (or stopped) instance of an image — a process tree wrapped in namespaces, cgroups, capabilities, and a layered filesystem (image's lowerdirs + a writable upperdir). Has an id, optional name, status, exit code, networks, mounts, log driver. The unit `docker ps` lists; the unit `docker run` creates.

name: Image
description: A read-only template comprising an ordered stack of layers + a config blob (entrypoint, env, exposed ports, default user). Identified by a content-addressable digest (sha256:…) and 0+ tag references. The thing `docker pull`/`docker build` produces and `docker run` consumes. Stored under `/var/lib/docker/<storage-driver>/` (classic) or `/var/lib/containerd/` (containerd image store).

name: Image layer
description: One unit in an image's stacked rootfs — corresponds to one Dockerfile instruction (FROM, RUN, COPY, ADD). Stored as a tarball under the storage driver's diff dir. Identified by a sha256 digest of its uncompressed content (diff_id). Layers are deduplicated across images; pulling a new image only fetches layers not already on disk.

name: Volume
description: Docker-managed persistent storage outside any container's writable layer. Created via `docker volume create` or implicitly by `docker run -v name:/path`. Stored under `/var/lib/docker/volumes/<name>/_data/`. Persists across container removal (unless container created with `--rm` and volume is anonymous). Preferred over bind mounts for portability — works the same on Linux/Windows hosts.

name: Named volume
description: A volume with an explicit user-given name (`docker volume create my-vol` or `docker run -v my-vol:/data`). Survives container removal indefinitely; must be removed explicitly via `docker volume rm` or pruned via `docker volume prune`.

name: Anonymous volume
description: A volume without a user-given name — Docker generates a random uuid. Created when `docker run -v /path` (no name before colon) or `--mount type=volume,dst=/path` (no src). Removed automatically only when the creating container was started with `--rm`. Otherwise must be pruned explicitly (`docker volume prune`); easy to leak.

name: Bind mount
description: Direct mount of a host-fs path into a container, bypassing Docker-managed storage. Specified via `--mount type=bind,src=<host-path>,dst=<container-path>` or `-v <host-path>:<container-path>`. Best for sharing source code in dev or sharing host config files (`/etc/resolv.conf`-style). Failure mode: with `-v`, missing host path is auto-created as a directory; with `--mount`, missing host path errors out unless `bind-create-src` is set.

name: tmpfs mount
description: In-memory mount; data lives in container memory and is destroyed when the container stops. `--mount type=tmpfs,dst=/path` or `--tmpfs /path`. Configurable via `tmpfs-size` (bytes) and `tmpfs-mode` (octal). For non-persistent state — caches, runtime files — that you don't want hitting the writable layer (avoids storage-driver overhead for hot paths).

name: Mount point
description: The container-side path where a volume / bind / tmpfs is attached, plus its mode (RW or RO), driver, propagation. Surfaced as the `Mounts[]` array in `docker inspect`. Each mount point records `Type` (volume/bind/tmpfs), `Source` (host path or volume mountpoint), `Destination` (container path), `Mode`, `RW`, `Propagation`.

name: Network (engine-perspective)
description: A Docker-managed network endpoint a container attaches to. From the engine's point of view, just a logical attachment with an id, driver name, and per-container IP/MAC. The on-host implementation (linux-bridge, vxlan, ipvlan parent interface, iptables chains) lives in docker/networking. Engine surfaces it via `--network`, `docker network ls`, and the `NetworkSettings` block of `docker inspect`.

name: Image tag
description: A mutable human-readable name pointing at an image digest, e.g. `nginx:1.27`, `myapp:latest`. Stored in the daemon's image-reference index. `docker pull` resolves a tag to a digest; the tag-to-digest mapping can change (the registry may push a new image to the same tag) — the same `docker pull nginx:latest` two days apart can fetch different bytes. Pin to digests for reproducibility.

name: Container process (pid 1)
description: The first process inside a container's pid namespace — what the entrypoint+cmd resolve to. By default, signals to the container (`docker stop`) go only to pid 1; if pid 1 doesn't propagate them, child processes don't see SIGTERM and the 10s grace period elapses to a SIGKILL. With `--init`, docker-init becomes pid 1 and forwards signals + reaps zombies.

name: Storage driver
description: The pluggable component that manages how image layers and the container writable layer are stored on disk for the legacy 'classic' image store. Configured via daemon.json `storage-driver`. Drivers: overlay2 (default for upgraded installs), fuse-overlayfs (rootless fallback pre-5.11 kernels), btrfs, zfs, vfs (no copy-on-write — only for testing/debug), windowsfilter (Windows). Switching requires daemon stop, data-root migration. Docker Engine 29.0+ uses containerd snapshotters by default for fresh installs.

name: overlay2 storage driver
description: Default classic storage driver on most Linux distros. Uses kernel OverlayFS to union-mount image layers (lowerdir, read-only) under a per-container writable layer (upperdir). Requires kernel ≥ 4.0 (RHEL/CentOS 3.10.0-514). Supports xfs (with d_type=true / ftype=1) and ext4. Up to 128 lower layers. Stores data under `/var/lib/docker/overlay2/<id>/{lower,merged,upper,work,diff,link}`. Page-cache shared across containers — memory-efficient. Copy-up on first write of an image-layer file.

name: vfs storage driver
description: Storage driver of last resort. No copy-on-write — every layer is a full copy. Massive disk usage, slow. Works on any filesystem (no kernel features required). Use only for debugging or environments where no other driver is supported.

name: btrfs storage driver
description: Storage driver using btrfs subvolumes/snapshots for layer separation. Requires `/var/lib/docker/` to live on a btrfs filesystem. Block-level CoW; better than overlay2 for write-heavy workloads but requires significant memory tuning.

name: zfs storage driver
description: Storage driver using zfs datasets/snapshots for layers. Requires `/var/lib/docker/` on a zfs filesystem. Block-level CoW. Good for high-density (PaaS) workloads. Requires substantial RAM (ZFS ARC).

name: devicemapper storage driver
description: Legacy block-level storage driver using LVM thin provisioning (devmapper-thinpool). Once the only RHEL/CentOS option pre-overlay2 on old kernels. Mostly retired; tunables `dm.basesize`, `dm.thinpooldev` retained for legacy installs.

name: Logging driver
description: Pluggable component that consumes container stdout/stderr. Default is json-file (no rotation — disk-fill foot-gun); local recommended for new installs. Configured per-daemon via daemon.json `log-driver` + `log-opts`, overridable per-container via `--log-driver` + `--log-opt`. Drivers: json-file, local, journald, syslog, fluentd, gelf, awslogs, splunk, etwlogs, gcplogs, none.

name: json-file logging driver
description: Default logging driver. Caches container logs as JSON under `/var/lib/docker/containers/<id>/<id>-json.log`. Each line is a JSON object with `{log, stream, time}`. Default has NO rotation — daemon never trims the file; long-running containers can fill the disk. Set `max-size` and `max-file` log-opts to enable rotation. Stays default for backwards compat with Kubernetes.

name: local logging driver
description: Recommended replacement for json-file. Performs log rotation by default (max-size=20m, max-file=5, compress=true). Uses a more efficient binary file format. Same `docker logs` UX as json-file. Doesn't ship a separate read API beyond the daemon's.

name: journald logging driver
description: Sends container logs to the host's systemd-journald. Each entry tagged with container_id, container_name. Filterable via `journalctl CONTAINER_NAME=…`. `docker logs` still works (daemon reads journal). Useful when the host already centralizes logs via journald.

name: fluentd logging driver
description: Forwards container logs to a Fluentd daemon over forward protocol. Requires fluentd reachable at `fluentd-address` (default localhost:24224). `fluentd-async=true` decouples container start from fluentd availability. Optional buffer with `fluentd-buffer-limit`, retry policy via `fluentd-max-retries` + `fluentd-retry-wait`. `docker logs` does NOT work for containers using fluentd — daemon doesn't keep a local cache.

name: syslog logging driver
description: Sends logs to a syslog daemon (local socket or remote tcp/udp/tls endpoint). Configured via `syslog-address`, `syslog-facility`, `syslog-format` (rfc5424 vs rfc3164). TLS via `syslog-tls-ca-cert`, `syslog-tls-cert`, `syslog-tls-key`.

name: gelf logging driver
description: Sends container logs to a Graylog/Logstash-compatible endpoint over UDP/TCP using the GELF format. Configured via `gelf-address`, `gelf-compression-type`, `gelf-tcp-max-reconnect`, `gelf-tcp-reconnect-delay`.

name: none logging driver
description: Discards all container logs. `docker logs` returns nothing. Used when you intentionally don't want stdout captured (the application logs elsewhere, e.g., directly to a log shipper from inside the container).

name: Live restore
description: Daemon configuration `live-restore: true` (or `dockerd --live-restore`) that lets containers keep running across daemon restarts/upgrades. On daemon upgrade the running containers don't lose their network interfaces or storage mounts. Patch upgrades only (`YY.MM.x`); skipped major upgrades may break the daemon's reconnect. Daemon-options that change (bridge IP, graph driver) prevent the reconnect — containers must be stopped manually. Linux-only; Swarm services excluded.

name: User namespace remapping
description: Daemon option `userns-remap` mapping container root (uid 0) to a non-zero uid on the host. Reduces container-escape blast radius. Requires `/etc/subuid` + `/etc/subgid` entries. `userns-remap: default` uses `dockremap` user; `userns-remap: testuser` uses a named user. Bind-mounts and volumes get owned by the remapped uid — common foot-gun. Mutually exclusive with `--privileged`, `--ipc=host`, `--net=host`, `--pid=host` containers.

name: Experimental features flag
description: Daemon-level `experimental: true` (or `dockerd --experimental`) gating non-stable features. Examples: containerd image store on older versions, certain BuildKit/Buildx behaviors. Required for some `metrics-addr` features. Per-CLI counterpart used to live in `~/.docker/config.json` `experimental: enabled`.

name: Daemon metrics endpoint
description: Prometheus-compatible scrape endpoint on the daemon. Configured via daemon.json `metrics-addr` (e.g. `127.0.0.1:9323`). Exposes `engine_daemon_*`, `engine_*`, build, network metrics. Bound to loopback by default — exposing on `0.0.0.0` opens an information-leak surface; consider an SSH tunnel or reverse-proxy. Metric names are explicitly subject to change (active development).

name: IPv6 support
description: Linux-only. Enabled per-network via `docker network create --ipv6` or daemon-wide for the default bridge via daemon.json `ipv6: true` + `fixed-cidr-v6` (e.g. `2001:db8:1::/64`). `ip6tables: true` (default) controls iptables-based v6 packet filtering. `default-address-pools` defines pools for dynamic /64 allocation; without v6 pools, Docker falls back to ULA (`fd00::/8`-derived) addressing. Requires `ip6_tables` kernel module loaded (auto-loaded on most distros; needs `modprobe ip6_tables` inside DinD).

name: iptables management
description: Daemon-managed iptables rules for NAT, filtering, isolation between user-defined networks. Toggled via daemon.json `iptables: true` (default). Disabling means you own the rules — `docker run -p 80:80` won't actually publish without your DNAT. Detail-level chains (DOCKER, DOCKER-USER, DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-1/2) live in docker/networking. Engine perspective: a daemon switch, off by default risks no-network at all.

name: TLS / mTLS for daemon socket
description: Default daemon socket is the unprotected `/var/run/docker.sock` (root-equivalent for whoever can write to it). Listening on TCP without TLS = remote root. Enable TLS via daemon.json `tls`, `tlsverify`, `tlscacert`, `tlscert`, `tlskey` (or `dockerd --tls --tlsverify --tlscacert=… --tlscert=… --tlskey=…`). Default ports: 2376 with TLS, 2375 without. Client picks via `DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY` + `DOCKER_CERT_PATH`.

name: Default cgroup namespace mode
description: `default-cgroupns-mode` daemon-config controlling whether new containers get a private cgroup namespace (`private`) or share the host's (`host`). With cgroupv2-only kernels, private cgroupns is the modern default. Per-container override: `docker run --cgroupns=host|private`.

name: Init process injection
description: Daemon-level `init: true` (and `init-path` to swap the binary) injects docker-init / tini as pid 1 of every container so naive entrypoints get correct signal forwarding and zombie reaping. Per-container override: `docker run --init`.

name: OOM score adjustment
description: `oom-score-adjust` daemon-config sets dockerd's own kernel OOM-killer score (-1000..1000); `--oom-score-adj` per-container does the same for the container init. Lower = less likely to be killed by the OOM killer. Default 0; -500 commonly used to keep dockerd alive when host is under memory pressure.

name: Health check
description: Per-container probe defined either by HEALTHCHECK in the Dockerfile or via `--health-cmd` + `--health-interval`/`--health-retries`/`--health-timeout`/`--health-start-period`. Surfaces in `docker inspect --format '{{.State.Health.Status}}'` as starting/healthy/unhealthy. Compose `depends_on.<svc>.condition: service_healthy` builds on it.

name: Restart policy
description: Per-container daemon-managed restart behavior. `--restart no` (default), `on-failure[:N]`, `always`, `unless-stopped`. Restart is by the daemon, NOT the OCI runtime — if dockerd is down, restarts pause. With Swarm, the equivalent is `deploy.restart_policy` and is managed by the swarm orchestrator instead.

name: daemon.json
description: The Docker daemon configuration file. Linux: `/etc/docker/daemon.json`. Rootless Linux: `~/.config/docker/daemon.json` (honors `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). Windows: `C:\ProgramData\docker\config\daemon.json`. Plain JSON. Re-read on daemon (re)start; `systemctl reload docker` works for some keys (proxies, debug, log-level), full restart needed for others. Daemon refuses to start on invalid JSON OR when the same option is given both as a flag and in the file.

name: Docker root dir
description: The on-disk directory the daemon stores everything under. Default `/var/lib/docker/` (Linux) / `C:\ProgramData\docker\` (Windows). Configured via daemon.json `data-root` (formerly `graph`). Subdirs include `image/`, `<storage-driver>/`, `volumes/`, `containers/`, `network/`, `swarm/`, `tmp/`. With containerd image store, image layers live under `/var/lib/containerd/` instead.

name: docker.sock
description: The Unix domain socket the docker CLI talks to dockerd over. Default `/var/run/docker.sock`. Owned by `root:docker` typically; membership in the `docker` group = root-equivalent on the host (a container can be launched with the host fs bind-mounted). 'Got permission denied while trying to connect to the Docker daemon socket' = client uid not in `docker` group OR socket file's group is wrong.

name: containerd.sock
description: containerd's grpc socket (`/run/containerd/containerd.sock`). dockerd connects to it for container lifecycle ops. Diagnosing a 'docker daemon ok but containers won't start' often means inspecting this socket and the containerd logs separately.

name: Dockerfile
description: Build-recipe text file. Each instruction (FROM, RUN, COPY, ADD, CMD, ENTRYPOINT, ENV, ARG, LABEL, EXPOSE, VOLUME, USER, WORKDIR, HEALTHCHECK, ONBUILD, STOPSIGNAL, SHELL) becomes (potentially) one image layer. Engine perspective: the artifact `docker build`/`docker buildx build` consumes; full instruction surface is catalogued in docker/build-buildkit.

name: .dockerignore
description: Build-context exclusion file (gitignore-style). Pattern matched against the build context root before transmission to the daemon/builder. Critical for build performance — without it, `node_modules/`, `.git/`, etc. get sent over the socket and slow every build. Engine perspective: implicit; the build engine reads it.

name: Docker config dir (~/.docker/)
description: Per-user CLI config: `~/.docker/config.json` (auths, default plugins, experimental, credsStore), contexts (`~/.docker/contexts/`), daemon-cert-dir (`~/.docker/<host>/{ca,cert,key}.pem`). `DOCKER_CONFIG` env var overrides.

name: cgroup filesystem
description: `/sys/fs/cgroup/`. Where the kernel exposes cgroup controllers (cpu, memory, pids, blkio, freezer, devices). Docker creates a per-container cgroup under `/sys/fs/cgroup/<controller>/docker/<container-id>` (cgroup v1) or `/sys/fs/cgroup/<slice>/docker-<id>.scope` (cgroup v2 + systemd). Modify a container's resource limits at runtime by writing to these knobs (or use `docker update`).

name: OCI bundle config.json
description: The OCI runtime spec file dockerd writes per-container before invoking runc. Lives in the runtime bundle dir. Lists args, env, capabilities, namespaces, mounts, cgroups, hooks. Engine doesn't expose it directly; runc reads it. Detail in docker/runtime.

name: OCI state.json
description: Per-container runtime state OCI runtimes maintain. Returned by `runc state`. Surface stays in docker/runtime; engine consumes it indirectly through containerd's task service.

name: Linux namespace (engine usage)
description: Kernel isolation primitive Docker uses to give each container its own view of pids/networking/mounts/uts/ipc/users/cgroups/time. Per-container engine flags: `--pid=`, `--ipc=`, `--network=`, `--userns=`, `--cgroupns=` accept either a private namespace, `host` (share with the host), or `container:<id>` (share with another container). The container/host duality is the most common cause of 'pid 1 inside the container is not really pid 1 of the host' confusion.

name: cgroup v1
description: Legacy multi-hierarchy cgroup ABI. Per-controller subtrees (`/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu`, `…/memory`, etc.). Still in use on older distros; expected to be phased out. Engine resource flags map onto v1 controllers when v1 is active.

name: cgroup v2
description: Unified cgroup hierarchy at `/sys/fs/cgroup/` (single mount). Required by some recent features (memory.events psi, io.cost). Modern distros default to v2-only. Container resource limits (`--memory`, `--cpus`, `--pids-limit`) translate to v2 knobs.

name: Linux capability (engine usage)
description: Subdivision of root privileges. Docker drops most capabilities by default (drops include CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_SYS_MODULE). Re-add via `--cap-add=` (e.g., `--cap-add=NET_ADMIN` for tcpdump in container); drop further via `--cap-drop=ALL` + selective `--cap-add=`. `--privileged` ≈ all capabilities + access to host devices + AppArmor/Seccomp disabled.

name: seccomp profile (engine usage)
description: Kernel syscall filter applied to a container. Docker ships a default profile blocking ~50 syscalls. Override per-container via `--security-opt seccomp=<path-to-profile.json>` (or `unconfined`). Daemon-wide default switchable via daemon.json `seccomp-profile`. Profile schema (defaultAction, syscalls[], etc.) catalogued in docker/security.

name: AppArmor profile (engine usage)
description: LSM profile applied per container on AppArmor-enabled distros (Ubuntu, Debian). Docker generates a default profile; override via `--security-opt apparmor=<profile-name>`. Detail in docker/security.

name: SELinux label (engine usage)
description: On SELinux-enabled distros, the daemon-wide `selinux-enabled: true` (and per-container `--security-opt label=…`) controls how container processes and files are labeled. Bind-mount `:z` / `:Z` modifies host labels (shared / private). Bind-mounting system dirs with `:Z` can render the host inoperable.

name: pid 1 zombie reaping
description: On Linux, pid 1 must reap orphaned children — otherwise the kernel leaves <defunct> entries indefinitely (kernel pid table fills). Most app servers (`node`, `python`, `java`) don't expect to be pid 1 and don't reap. Symptom: thousands of <defunct> child processes inside the container, or apparent FD/process exhaustion. Fix: run with `--init` (docker-init/tini becomes pid 1 and reaps) or use a runtime like supervisord/systemd inside.

name: Container state: created
description: `docker container ls -a --filter status=created`. The container has been created (`docker create`) but not started. Has an id and config but no running process. Resources allocated; rootfs prepared; pid namespace not yet entered.

name: Container state: running
description: `status=running`. Container's pid 1 is alive. The default 'happy path' state. Reflected in `State.Running=true` of `docker inspect`.

name: Container state: paused
description: `status=paused`. Container processes frozen via cgroup freezer (v1) or cgroup.freeze (v2). Filesystem and network state preserved; processes don't run. `docker pause` / `docker unpause`. Rare in production; useful for snapshotting.

name: Container state: stopped
description: Filter alias — UI-side same as 'exited'. `State.Status=exited`, `State.Running=false`. Container's writable layer remains; restartable via `docker start`.

name: Container state: exited
description: `status=exited`. Process completed (cleanly or via signal). `State.ExitCode` populated. Common values: 0 (clean), 1 (generic error), 125 (docker daemon error pre-runtime), 126 (entrypoint not executable), 127 (entrypoint not found), 137 (SIGKILL — usually OOM), 139 (SIGSEGV), 143 (SIGTERM). Containers in this state still consume disk for their writable layer until removed.

name: Container state: dead
description: `status=dead`. Container partially-removed and unable to be stopped/started. Usually indicates a daemon bug or stuck mount. Mitigation: `docker rm -f <id>`; if that fails, restart the daemon.

name: OCI image format
description: The image format Docker has aligned to since 2017 (Docker manifest v2-2 ≈ OCI image spec). Two manifest forms: per-platform manifest (descriptor list of layer descriptors + config descriptor) and image index (multi-arch — descriptor list of per-platform manifests). Detail in docker/runtime; engine perspective is 'this is what `docker pull` retrieves and `docker image inspect` displays'.

name: Image layer digest
description: Content-addressable identifier for an image layer (`sha256:<hex>`). Two flavors: 'diff_id' (sha256 of the uncompressed tarball) and 'descriptor digest' (sha256 of the on-wire compressed blob). The pair is how the daemon dedupes layers across images and verifies pull integrity.

name: Content-addressable storage
description: The principle that an image / layer / blob is identified by the hash of its bytes. Two pulls of the same digest are guaranteed identical bits. Foundation for layer dedup, pull-cache, and signing. Tags are mutable references to digests; pinning to digests gives reproducibility tags can't.

name: Union filesystem
description: The technique behind layered images: stack N read-only directories under one writable directory and present a single merged view. Implementations: OverlayFS (overlay2 driver), btrfs/zfs subvolumes, devicemapper thin-provisioning. Performance characteristic: read of an unmodified file resolves through the lowerdirs; first write triggers copy-up to the upperdir.

name: Copy-on-write (CoW)
description: Pattern: shared read-only data; write triggers a private copy. Image layers are CoW. overlay2 copies the WHOLE FILE on first write (file-granular CoW), so writing a single byte in a 1GB log file copies the full GB to the upperdir. Block-level CoW drivers (btrfs/zfs) don't have this problem but have other ones. For write-heavy workloads, prefer volumes (bypass storage driver entirely).

name: Image pull policy
description: `docker run --pull` controls when to fetch the image: `missing` (default — pull if not present locally), `always` (always check the registry), `never` (use only local). Same semantics as Kubernetes `imagePullPolicy`. Critical for reproducible deploys (always vs missing) and air-gapped envs (never).

name: ENTRYPOINT vs CMD
description: ENTRYPOINT is the binary; CMD provides default arguments. `docker run <image>` runs `ENTRYPOINT CMD`. `docker run <image> bash` runs `ENTRYPOINT bash` (CMD is replaced). `docker run --entrypoint=sh <image>` overrides ENTRYPOINT to `sh`. Common confusion: shell-form (`CMD echo hi`) wraps in `/bin/sh -c`; exec-form (`CMD ["echo", "hi"]`) doesn't — only exec-form forwards signals correctly.

name: Signal propagation
description: `docker stop` sends SIGTERM (configurable via `--stop-signal` or Dockerfile STOPSIGNAL) to the container's pid 1, waits the grace period (`--stop-timeout`, default 10s), then SIGKILL. If pid 1 is a shell wrapping the real binary, the signal often goes to the shell, not the binary. Two fixes: exec-form ENTRYPOINT (`["binary"]`), or `--init` (docker-init forwards signals to all processes in the container's pgrp).

name: Container exit code
description: `docker inspect --format '{{.State.ExitCode}}' <id>`. Conventional codes: 0 success; 1 generic error; 125 daemon-side error before the entrypoint ran; 126 entrypoint exists but not executable; 127 entrypoint not found; 128+N indicates termination by signal N (137 = SIGKILL/OOM, 139 = SIGSEGV, 143 = SIGTERM). The most-asked production debugging question is 'why exit code 137' — answer is almost always cgroup memory limit hit (OOM-killer).

name: TTY allocation
description: `-t` / `--tty` allocates a pseudo-TTY for the container's stdio. Combined with `-i` / `--interactive`, gives an interactive shell. Without `-t`, output isn't line-buffered the same way and many programs detect they're not on a terminal and don't print colors / prompts. Detached (`-d`) containers don't get a TTY — `docker logs` reads from the captured streams.

name: Attached vs detached
description: `docker run` without `-d` attaches the CLI to the container's stdio — when the CLI exits, the container is sent SIGTERM. `docker run -d` runs detached; the CLI returns immediately and the container keeps running. `docker attach <id>` re-attaches an existing container (lossy: the attach might receive partial historical output). For long-lived stuff, prefer `-d` + `docker logs -f`.

name: Image tag mutability
description: Tags are mutable refs in registries. `nginx:latest` today and `nginx:latest` tomorrow can be different bytes. Reproducibility / supply-chain best practice: pin to digest (`nginx@sha256:…`). The daemon's local image cache mitigates this slightly — once pulled, your local tag points at a fixed digest until you re-pull.

name: Slim container image
description: A container image stripped of build tools, package managers, and shells — only the application binary and its runtime deps. Smaller (faster pulls, less network), more secure (smaller attack surface). Trade-off: missing `ps`, `cat`, `bash` etc. makes debugging hard. Counterstrategies: ephemeral debug sidecars sharing the target's pid/network namespace.

name: Distroless image
description: A class of slim images (gcr.io/distroless/*, Chainguard Images) with no shell, no package manager, no debug tools — only the language runtime + app. `docker exec -it <distroless> sh` fails with `OCI runtime exec failed: exec: "sh": executable file not found`. Debug variants (e.g. `gcr.io/distroless/nodejs:debug`) include busybox; pure ones require sidecar-based debugging.

name: Debug sidecar
description: A second container sharing the target container's namespaces (`--pid=container:<id>`, `--network=container:<id>`) used to bring in debug tooling without modifying the target. Pattern: `docker run -it --rm --pid=container:my-app --network=container:my-app nicolaka/netshoot bash` to run tcpdump/strace/ss against the slim target. iximiuz/cdebug automates this.

name: nicolaka/netshoot
description: De-facto-standard 'fat' debugging image: ip, ss, tcpdump, dig, nslookup, mtr, iperf, drill, ngrep, nmap, lsof, strace, busybox. Run as a debug sidecar to investigate slim containers, or to check networking from inside an overlay. Image at `nicolaka/netshoot`; ~50MB.

name: Docker build context
description: The directory tree the docker CLI sends to the daemon/builder when running `docker build .`. Filtered by `.dockerignore`. Engine perspective: streamed over the API; the size of the context is a real perf factor (slow build = wasted time on a 2GB context). Local context (`.`), URL contexts (`https://github.com/foo/bar.git#main:subdir`), stdin (`-`) all supported.

name: Image history
description: `docker history <image>` shows each layer with its created-by command and size. Useful to find the layer that bloated an image (e.g., a leaked apt cache, a forgotten temp file). When chasing 'why is this image 2GB', `docker history` + a known-good base = a 5-second diagnosis.
